summary: Staples everyone knows (rice, beef, chicken, corn, wheat, milk), so a casual player clears or nearly clears it: too easy for Today's list, a deep and friendly Blitz where almost every food scores.
reasons: Three casual orders found 10, 10 and 7: grains and meats are gimmes, and lives go on fruit and cash crops (coffee #44, sugarcane #12, tomatoes #11, apples, bananas), each with a figure. A 90 s Blitz scored 23 of 28; only carrots, oats, cocoa, turkey and fish (outside FAO's 50) missed.

FAO 2016 is fine for a Blitz: the year is in the prompt and the pool of the 48 biggest farm products barely changes in a decade. Not for Today's list, where the order is the game: Wikipedia tags the table a decade old (Aug 2026) and newer FAO figures reportedly put milk ahead of rice (not checked).

Category words alone (meat, grain, dairy, poultry, cereal, livestock, crops, fruit, vegetables) hand over no top-10 answer. Cattle, cow, pig and hen give Beef, Pork and Chicken, which is fair: they are FAO's own item names.
fixes: "beet" offers "Did you mean Beef?" and "hay" offers "Did you mean Pork?" (through the alias "ham"): both are real farm words and should be free, not corrected into top-10 answers.

"meat" alone offers "Did you mean Goat meat?" (#22), "fruit" offers Oil palm fruit and "seeds" Sunflower seeds: a bare category word should be free or "be more specific", not a correction to one row (in Blitz it would score).
"chicken egg" offers Chicken, not Eggs: add the singular "chicken egg" to Eggs (only "chicken eggs" is there).
Refresh when Wikipedia has a newer year of FAO's gross production value (the page says its data is for 2016).
